items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Its worse than a shame that a guy like Paul Whiteman who could hardly hold a violin was known as the King of Jazz at the time when Fletcher could have made him wish that he had never heard the word jazz.

ctx.x: they left Fletcher play. That was one night that I thought the public was very unfair because I knew and we all knew that although we had a good band, we were really not in the class of Fletcher.

And when Fletcher did start to play, I came back on our bandstand to listen to them and after that it was hard for us to play for two reasons. One was that Fletcher had scored with the public which wanted more from him when they had finished their set and the second reason was because we had lost the battle and really did not want to play any more although we still tried, but there was not much fight left in us. Without a doubt Fletcher Henderson had the greatest dance orchestra in the world, before, then and…

Another thing that was a thrill for me at the Savoy was the masked ball once every year. The first one we played was called 'Arabian Nights' and the second 'South Sea Island'. There was also a big ball once a year called 'Female Impersonators Ball'. We called it the 'fag ball' as these sort of individuals were called faggots or sissies, which would make it a sissies ball.
